input: This appraisal examines the financial case for installing a solar array, drawing together the capital cost, the anticipated savings, and the time value of money in order to assess whether the project creates value. The installed cost of the array is put at $633k, payable at the outset. Against this outlay, the array is expected to deliver a net saving estimated at $155k per year, and this saving is projected to continue for a period of 12 years, corresponding to the appraisal horizon adopted here. In order to compare money arising at different times on a like-for-like basis, the stream of savings is discounted at a rate of 8%, which brings the total present value of the savings to $1168k. Set against the installed cost of $633k, this yields a net present value of $535k, a positive figure which indicates that, on the estimates adopted, the project more than recovers its cost in present-value terms. It should nevertheless be borne in mind that the savings figures underpinning the appraisal are vendor and utility estimates, and that no saving has yet been measured on a comparable installation; consequently, the net present value of $535k is only as reliable as those estimates themselves, and the position should be revisited once metered data from the first year of operation become available.
target:
The solar array should be approved on the stated figures: the appraisal gives a net present value of $535k against an installed cost of $633k. The expected net saving is $155k per year for 12 years. At a discount rate of 8%, the present value of the savings is $1168k; set against the installed cost of $633k, the net present value is $535k.

The discount rate is the rate the business applies to its other capital appraisals, so the array is judged on the same terms as the projects it competes with for funds. The savings are vendor and utility estimates, and no saving has yet been measured on a comparable installation. Every figure after the installed cost rests on those estimates: the annual saving, the period over which the saving is held level, and the generation behind both. The installed cost is the only figure in the appraisal fixed by quotation rather than estimated from performance. A shortfall in the saving reduces the present value in proportion, and the appraisal states no margin because the estimates carry no measured spread. Approval on these figures is approval of an estimate, recorded as such. The first year of metered operation sets the saving against which the remaining years are judged, and the appraisal is reopened if that figure falls short of the estimate.
